open_obligations.what_is_open: Necessity and sufficiency of the proposed finite structural atlas on every mixed-support design-A and design-B fiber.
open_obligations.obstruction: The result requires exhaustiveness of the mixed-support elimination in the sibling-owned open-ended question. The established all-rank-two orientation boxes and conditional residual-forest reduction do not show that inactive rows, coincident endpoints, forced zeros, and all real algebraic support-face components are exhausted. Generic two-copy quantifier elimination would decide constancy but would not prove the claimed structural classifier.
open_obligations.attempted: Extended the established cycle-to-SCM image equality, all-rank-two orientation classification, and residual-margin forest elimination to every branch they cover, and checked where their arguments stop at rank-one and inactive-row degeneracies.
open_obligations.partial_result:
By the established cycle-to-SCM lift, the two full-SCM target images are exactly
\[
\mathcal T_A(p,m)
=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},
\qquad
\mathcal T_B(p)
=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}.
\]
Consequently, constancy of \(\tau\) on either full fiber is equivalent to constancy of \(\tau_C\) on the corresponding cycle fiber.  If two cycle points have different \(\tau_C\)-values, their lifts are legal full SCMs with the same observables and, in design A, the same supplied margins; the lift permits boundary mechanisms, while an interior cycle pair gives strictly positive twins.  On the all-rank-two design-A branch, the established orientation theorem enumerates at most \(2^4\) closed endpoint boxes and gives a necessary-and-sufficient within-box and cross-box target-agreement test.  For design B, the established residual-forest theorem eliminates the positive unknown margins conditional on \((b,a,\rho)\): at every response type the two incident residuals either both vanish or are nonzero and negatively proportional, active links propagate positive margin ratios, every active cycle has product one, component scales satisfy normalization, and the relevance inequality is then checked.  Thus the claimed rigidity and legal-twin conclusions hold on these completed branches.  What is not derived is exhaustion of all mixed-rank, inactive-row, coincident-endpoint, and forced-zero support faces by the proposed structural chart list.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Universal coverage of every singular and boundary observable law by the same global structural atlas.
open_obligations.obstruction: The published regular formula agrees with the cycle target, and the explicit forced-zero rank-two datum is certified, but the universal boundary clause is equivalent to exhaustiveness of the unresolved mixed-support chart list.
open_obligations.attempted: Matched the published regular PN/PS functional to the cycle target through the established lift, isolated the certified forced-zero boundary branch, and applied the residual-forest theorem to the conditional design-B margin problem.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\) denote the pair computed by Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33) of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki on their regular domain.  The cited regular-identification result gives, for every compatible SCM satisfying their Conditions 1--3,
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p).
\]
The established cycle-to-SCM lift gives \(\tau(\vartheta)=\tau_C(b,a)\), so every compatible cycle point covered by those conditions has the same value \(R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\).  Hence any rigid atlas value on that regular domain must agree with the published formula.  Separately, the established explicit boundary theorem proves for the forced-zero datum
\[
\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing,
\qquad
\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\},
\]
and the established residual-forest theorem exactly eliminates design-B margins conditional on each proposed cycle chart.  These facts verify regular-domain agreement and the displayed boundary branch, but not the assertion that the same structural chart list exhausts every singular or boundary observable law.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Attribution of the unique design-B overlap value to the global compiler on every Kawakami-regular law.
open_obligations.obstruction: Kawakami's cited simultaneous equations identify the conditional response-type weights, and the explicit boundary singularity and singleton target are established, but universal output by the named compiler still requires the unresolved mixed-support exhaustiveness theorem.
open_obligations.attempted: Derived the PN/PS transformation directly from response-type incidence, proved exact column dependence of both explicit proxy-loading matrices, and reused the established singleton boundary calculation.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Under \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}(P_{\vartheta})\), the cited Kawakami theorem identifies \(\omega_0^{\mathrm K}\) and \(\omega_1^{\mathrm K}\).  In the ordering \((00,01,10,11)\), the event \(X=1,Y=1\) admits precisely types \(01\) and \(11\), whereas \(X=0,Y=0\) admits precisely types \(00\) and \(01\).  Therefore response consistency gives
\[
\mathrm{PN}(\vartheta)
=\frac{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,2}}
       {\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,2}+\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,4}},
\qquad
\mathrm{PS}(\vartheta)
=\frac{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,2}}
       {\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,1}+\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,2}},
\]
whenever the conditioning-event probabilities, which are the displayed denominators, are positive.  Thus
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=\phi_{\mathrm K}(\omega_0^{\mathrm K},\omega_1^{\mathrm K}).
\]
For the explicit boundary datum, each row of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) equals
\[
(1,b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_1),b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_2),b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_3)).
\]
Since \(b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}\in\Delta_{\{w_1,w_2,w_3\}}\), its entries sum to one.  Hence the first column of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is the sum of its last three columns, so \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is singular for both \(x=0\) and \(x=1\).  The established boundary theorem gives
\[
\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing,
\qquad
\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}.
\]
This proves the target transformation and the one-law strict scope separation.  Attribution of every unique overlap value to the unfinished global structural compiler still depends on mixed-support exhaustiveness.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Termination, chart-count, algebraic-degree, and rational certificate-size bounds for the specific structural compiler.
open_obligations.obstruction: Without a complete mixed-support structural enumeration there is no finite list whose chart number, elimination degree, or coefficient growth can be bounded. A generic real-algebraic decision bound applies to the raw fiber but violates the theorem's stated method.
open_obligations.attempted: Counted the fixed-alphabet raw variables, constraints, and degrees, and verified termination of the completed rank-two and residual-forest branches.
open_obligations.partial_result: For fixed \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), the normalized cycle equations contain finitely many real variables and finitely many polynomial equalities and inequalities.  After one redundant coordinate is removed from each simplex, their numbers are bounded by \(C_0(k\ell+k+\ell)\) for a universal constant \(C_0\), and their degrees are at most two before residual proportionality is eliminated.  The established all-rank-two branch terminates by enumerating at most \(2^4\) orientations and then performing finitely many linear-algebra and order tests over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  The established residual-forest branch terminates by finitely many residual-zero, signed-ratio, forest-propagation, cycle-product, normalization, and relevance tests.  Generic real-algebraic decision and sampling applied to the raw fixed-alphabet fiber would yield a terminating doubly exponential envelope, but it would be the forbidden generic classifier rather than the stated structural compiler.  Because the mixed-support structural enumeration is not yet proved exhaustive, neither its chart count nor its algebraic-degree and rational bit-size bounds have been derived.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Unconditional correctness of the deterministic chart selector for the claimed atlas on every separated rigid stratum.
open_obligations.obstruction: The multinomial delta-method and Wald calculations close after local chart exhaustiveness is known. Until mixed-support exhaustion is proved, an omitted incident or nearby incompatible component can invalidate the selector claim.
open_obligations.attempted: Completed the chart-distance, slack-continuity, common-Jacobian Taylor expansion, sandwich consistency, positive-definiteness, Wald-coverage, and fallback calculations conditional on local exhaustiveness.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Conditional on local exhaustiveness of the finite certified atlas, independent multinomial sampling and proportional independent margin sampling give
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_{\zeta}),
\qquad
\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}.
\]
For an incident chart \(\chi\), the definition of distance to its closed domain and the fact that \(\zeta\) belongs to that closure imply
\[
d_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)
\le \|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2
=O_P(n^{-1/2})
=o_P(t_n),
\qquad t_n=n^{-1/4}.
\]
Continuity of \(\eta_{\chi}\) and \(\eta_{\chi}(\zeta)\ge\varepsilon\) make the slack test pass with probability tending to one, while distance at least \(\varepsilon\) from each incompatible chart closure makes every incompatible distance test fail with probability tending to one.  The common value and Jacobian on incident charts and their twice continuously differentiable extensions give
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)
=J_{\chi}(\zeta)\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)+o_P(1).
\]
Thus the continuous mapping theorem yields the stated Gaussian limit, and continuity of the sandwich map yields \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}V_{\tau}\).  The lower eigenvalue bound \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\) implies eventual positive definiteness and ordinary Wald coverage.  The fallback identities follow directly from the definitions.  This closes the asymptotic calculation once the incident chart family is locally exhaustive; that last premise is not yet available from the unresolved global atlas theorem.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Uniform first-order Hausdorff equivalence between the exact confidence-fiber inversion and the selected Wald ellipse for the globally defined atlas.
open_obligations.obstruction: Exact coverage does not require rank stability, but the global Hausdorff assertion requires both a uniform glued-chart likelihood expansion and proof that no mixed-support component is omitted near the true law.
open_obligations.attempted: Proved exact Berger--Boos coverage from the preliminary-region event and discrete super-uniform tail values, and reduced the separated smooth local case to the profile-Wald quadratic conditional on atlas exhaustiveness.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(q_0\) be the true observable law and let \(t_0=\tau(\vartheta)\).  Exact inversion of each binomial tail and the stated Bonferroni allocation imply
\[
P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}\le\beta_n.
\]
For a fixed compatible pair \((q,t)\), put
\[
G_{q,t}
=P_q\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)\ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\}.
\]
The randomized variable is not needed: the ordinary upper-tail value is super-uniform even at atoms, so
\[
P_q\{G_{q,t}\le u\}\le u,
\qquad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Because \(t_0\in\mathcal T(q_0)\), on \(\{q_0\in C_n\}\) the supremum defining \(\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)\) includes \(q_0\), whence
\[
\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)
\ge\min\{1,\beta_n+G_{q_0,t_0}\}.
\]
Using \(\beta_n\le\alpha/2\), it follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{q_0}\{t_0\notin K_n\}
&\le P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}
  +P_{q_0}\{G_{q_0,t_0}\le\alpha-\beta_n\}\\
&\le\beta_n+(\alpha-\beta_n)=\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves exact finite-sample coverage and remains valid along arbitrary sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\).  On a locally exhaustive separated smooth chart, the multinomial likelihood has the usual uniform quadratic expansion, and the common incident Jacobian reduces the target profile to the Wald quadratic; this gives \(\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\xrightarrow{P}0\) under that local premise.  The stated global Hausdorff conclusion still requires a uniform glued-chart profile expansion and proof that no mixed-support component is omitted near the true law.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(\pi_i=P_{\vartheta}(U=i)\) for \(i\in\{1,2,3,4\}\).  We first verify that every conditional probability appearing in the claim is defined.  Membership \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\), the definition \(p_{ewz}=P_{\vartheta}(E=e,W=w,Z=z\mid S=1)\), and the local condition \(P_{\vartheta}(S=1)=1\) give
\[
 P_{\vartheta}(E=e)
 =P_{\vartheta}(E=e\mid S=1)
 =\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}p_{ewz}
 =r_e.
\]
By selected-table positivity and the nonemptiness of the finite alphabets, \(r_e>0\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\).  In particular,
\[
 P_{\vartheta}(X=1)\ge P_{\vartheta}(E=11)=r_{11}>0,
 \qquad
 P_{\vartheta}(X=0)\ge P_{\vartheta}(E=00)=r_{00}>0,
\]
and hence
\[
 P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)
 =\frac{r_{11}}{r_{11}+r_{10}}>0,
 \qquad
 P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)
 =\frac{r_{00}}{r_{00}+r_{01}}>0.
\]

By response consistency and the stated encoding of \(U\), under \(X=1\) the event \(Y=1\) occurs exactly when \(U\in\{1,2\}\), while under \(X=0\) the event \(Y=1\) occurs exactly when \(U\in\{1,3\}\), and the event \(Y=0\) occurs exactly when \(U\in\{2,4\}\).  The local independence \(X\perp U\), together with the just-established positivity of both treatment arms, therefore yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)
 &=P_{\vartheta}(U\in\{1,2\}\mid X=1)=\pi_1+\pi_2,\\
 P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)
 &=P_{\vartheta}(U\in\{1,3\}\mid X=0)=\pi_1+\pi_3,\\
 P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)
 &=P_{\vartheta}(U\in\{2,4\}\mid X=0)=\pi_2+\pi_4.
\end{aligned}
\]
The local restriction \(P_{\vartheta}(U=3)=0\) says \(\pi_3=0\), so
\[
 P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)=\pi_2.
\]
For type \(2\), response consistency gives \(Y=1\) when \(X=1\) and \(Y=0\) when \(X=0\).  Thus independence of \(X\) and \(U\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{PN}(\vartheta)
 &=P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=1,Y=1)\\
 &=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(U=2,Y=1\mid X=1)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)}
 =\frac{P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=1)}{\pi_1+\pi_2}
 =\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_1+\pi_2}\\
 &=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)},
\end{aligned}
\]
and, similarly,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{PS}(\vartheta)
 &=P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=0,Y=0)\\
 &=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(U=2,Y=0\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)}
 =\frac{P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=0)}{\pi_2+\pi_4}
 =\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_2+\pi_4}\\
 &=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the displayed pair for the particular restricted SCM \(\vartheta\).

By the definition of the design-A target set, membership \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) implies
\[
 \tau(\vartheta)\in
 \{\tau(\widetilde\vartheta):\widetilde\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\}
 =\mathcal T_A(p,m).
\]
Consequently, if \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\), its unique element is \(\tau(\vartheta)\), which is the displayed pair.

For completeness, the local restrictions on this one member do not themselves force rigidity of its unrestricted fiber.  Here is an explicit witness.  Write \(M=\lvert\mathcal W\rvert\) and \(K=\lvert\mathcal Z\rvert\).  In both SCMs below take \(b_i(w)=1/M\), \(g_i(z)=1/K\), and \(s_e=1\) for every admissible \(i,w,z,e\).  For the first SCM take
\[
 (\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_3,\pi_4)=\left(\frac13,\frac13,0,\frac13\right),
 \qquad e_i(z)=\frac12
\]
for every \(i,z\).  It satisfies \(S=1\) almost surely, \(X\perp U\), and \(P(U=3)=0\).  Directly applying the four response maps gives
\[
 (m_{11},m_{01},m_{10},m_{00})
 =\left(\frac13,\frac16,\frac16,\frac13\right),
 \qquad
 p_{ewz}=\frac{m_e}{MK}>0,
\]
and its target is \(\tau=(1/2,1/2)\).  For the second SCM take the same proxy and selection mechanisms but set
\[
 (\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_3,\pi_4)
 =\left(\frac13,\frac14,\frac16,\frac14\right)
\]
and, independently of \(z\), set
\[
 (e_1(z),e_2(z),e_3(z),e_4(z))
 =\left(\frac34,\frac13,\frac12,\frac13\right).
\]
The contributions of types \((1,2)\) to cell \(11\) are \((1/4,1/12)\); those of types \((1,3)\) to cell \(01\) are \((1/12,1/12)\); those of types \((3,4)\) to cell \(10\) are \((1/12,1/12)\); and those of types \((2,4)\) to cell \(00\) are \((1/6,1/6)\).  Hence this second SCM has exactly the same \(m\) and the same positive selected table \(p_{ewz}=m_e/(MK)\), while
\[
 \tau=\left(\frac{1/12}{1/3},\frac{1/6}{1/3}\right)
 =\left(\frac14,\frac12\right).
\]
All displayed weights and assignment probabilities are nonnegative and normalized; the uniform conditional proxy mechanisms satisfy proxy exclusion, and constant selection satisfies outcome-dependent selection.  Thus both parameters are legal members of the same design-A fiber, but their targets differ.  This proves that imposing the three local restrictions on the singled-out \(\vartheta\) supplies a validation identity, not rigidity of the unrestricted fiber.  The restrictions are used only after membership in the main design has been assumed and therefore are local hypotheses of this corollary, not additional defining assumptions of either main design.
